category_note: Conceptually this is a logo-reveal/brand-lockup sting (typographic chaos resolving into the FREE STYLE LAB wordmark, with scale-punch + glow on landing). Classified as kinetic-type instead because logo-reveal's contract expects a supplied logo asset (`content.logo: <asset path>`, `asset_needs` = a logo `source`), and there is none here — the site has no exported logo image/SVG, only styled live text defined in CSS (font-family + two hex colors). Since text is the hero and the piece is fully asset-free, kinetic-type's `scenes[]` shape is the correct fit; the settle beat borrows logo-reveal vocabulary (`glow` bloom, `scale_punch`/press-release landing) rather than the `logo-outro` block, since that block expects a real logo element to assemble/mask.
style: Freestyle/battle urban energy, confident but not aggressive (the aggressive register is reserved for a later 'Modo Bestia' clip in this series). Typographic chaos-to-order: a rapid 9-font identity cycle that reads as searching/battling for form, snapping into the calm, settled brand lockup on landing. Dark stage with subtle radial color bleed, like stage lighting.

customize.reuse_summary: No catalog block matches a multi-face typeface-cycle build-up (catalog-map.md's kinetic-typo row only lists the 18 caption-* blocks, none of which do font-family substitution) — confirmed gap, hand-authored. Two hyperframes-animation RULES are reused (not invented) for the underlying mechanics: `discrete-text-sequence` drives the whole-shot state array (9 font/scale swaps + the final landing state, all whole-state jumps at time thresholds — exactly the rule's documented scope per rules-index.md: 'hard-cut / flash word swaps, in-place token cycle, whole-line state swaps at time thresholds → discrete-text-sequence'); `press-release-spring` is reused for the landing scale-punch+glow because the wordmark is already resting on screen when it lands (a reaction, not an arrival-from-nothing — `spring-pop-entrance` was considered and rejected for this reason per its own doc: 'distinct from press-release-spring — a click/press → release feedback chain on an element that already rests on screen'). The `kinetic-type-beats` blueprint's shot-structure philosophy (Scene1 first-beat-lands / Scene2..N beats-replace-in-place / SceneN resolve-and-hold, `kinetic-type-to-logo-reveal` Hook role) is borrowed for pacing/scene-shape, not copy-pasted verbatim (no sub-variant covers a 9-face cycle). `ambient-glow-bloom` was considered for the landing glow and rejected in favor of applying motion-vocabulary's plain `glow` primitive (`filter:drop-shadow` pulse) directly on the type, because the wordmark text is itself the glow source (site reference below) — ambient-glow-bloom's separate backing-halo layer is built for a card/logo hero, not gradient-fill type.
customize.fidelity_source: BRIEF.md's Notes section already summarizes the relevant palette/gradients; to nail exact numbers for the parts director.md Part 2 must design (background gradient recipe, the 9-font scale-compensation table, and the landing scale-punch/glow curve) I cross-referenced the live site's own CSS/JS at C:\Users\asfura\Desktop\freestyle-lab-html\index.html (the splash screen this clip reproduces) — not a scrape for new content, just reading the exact values the site already uses so the recreation is pixel/timing-accurate. Cited by line number below.

layout.canvas: 1080x1920, hero-frame, flex column centered both axes
layout.wordmark_structure:
ONE persistent two-line element, unchanged in DOM shape across both scenes — only font-family/scale/color update. Line 1: 'FREE' + 'STYLE' as one word 'FREESTYLE' (STYLE is an inline span for independent color control). Line 2: 'LAB'. This reconciles the draft's scene text ('FREESTYLE LAB' cycle vs 'FREE STYLE LAB' settle, which read like 3 separate words) against the actual site markup at index.html:749 — `
Freestyle
Lab
` — a single wordmark, 'style' is a colored substring of 'Freestyle', not its own word. Kept as one continuous element (no scene-to-scene DOM swap) so there is zero layout reflow at the 1.8s cut — only the font/scale/color state changes, which is also cheaper and matches 'single wordmark held center-stage' in the original brief.
layout.type_size: --sp-base: clamp(64px, 15vw, 132px) scaled up from the site's web clamp(40px,13vw,84px) for full-bleed 1080x1920 video legibility (per typography.md's in-feed/full-screen sizing guidance); actual rendered size = sp-base * per-font scale (see sequence below)
layout.safe_margins: ≥120px each side; wordmark never exceeds ~85% canvas width at any cycle font (Anton, the widest at scale 1, is the sizing anchor)

radials.label: pink, top
radials.size_ref: 900px 520px at the site's viewport — scale proportionally to canvas (~83% canvas width x 27% canvas height)

background.note: Very low opacity (.06-.16) so the wordmark stays the hero — matches the site's own hero background exactly, per BRIEF.md Notes. The site's full body bg has a 4th near-duplicate pink layer at 50% 108% (index.html:24); omitted here since BRIEF.md's Notes section names only 3 gradients — optional for the Builder to add if the bottom of frame reads too empty at 9:16.

cycle_sequence.engine: discrete-text-sequence (sparse {t, state} array, reverse-search per frame, INSTANT jumps — no crossfade between fonts, per the rule's core constraint)
cycle_sequence.note: scale factors below are the site's own per-font compensation table (index.html:2304-2308) — each display face has different intrinsic width/x-height, so a flat font-size swap makes the wordmark visibly grow/shrink face to face; the scale keeps apparent size roughly constant across the cycle.

states.event: hard-cut into landing state — triggers landing_motion below

cycle_sequence.color_during_cycle: text stays neutral throughout (paper gradient #F2EEF7 -> #cfc6dc top-to-bottom, background-clip:text, matching index.html:533) — the 'STYLE' span inherits the same gradient, no color split yet; the swap reads by SHAPE not color, exactly per the draft's original intent

per_swap_jitter.primitive: motion-vocabulary `shake`, scaled down from its default to a faint sell of instability per the draft brief ('faint per-swap shake or 1-2px jitter')
per_swap_jitter.recipe: gsap keyframes [{x:-1.5},{x:1.5},{x:0}], ease:none, duration ~0.08s, fired at each of the 9 swap onsets (t = 0, 0.2, 0.4 ... 1.6). NOT fired on the 1.8s landing cut — that transition uses landing_motion instead, a shake there would fight the press-release settle.

landing.markup_note: same element as the cycle, no new DOM — only font-family, --sp-scale, and the STYLE span's color change

landing_motion.rule: press-release-spring, mapped to the site's exact sp-lock @keyframes (index.html:542-547) rather than the rule's generic PRESS_SCALE/RELEASE_DUR defaults — using the literal site curve for 1:1 fidelity since this is a recreation, not a fresh design:

timeline.note: press/dip — arrives already compressed at the hard-cut instant (no separate linear press-in tween needed; the cut itself lands here)
settle — 100% keyframe, 0.5s total duration after the 1.8s cut

landing_motion.easing: cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1) as ONE continuous curve across all 3 stops (matches the site's single CSS @keyframes animation) — if the Builder's GSAP timeline needs two discrete tweens instead, use power1.in for 1.8->2.08 and back.out(1.6) for 2.08->2.3 as the press-release-spring equivalent, RELEASE_START = 2.08 exactly adjacent to the press tween's end so scale continuity holds

glow.primitive: motion-vocabulary `glow`, implemented as filter:drop-shadow (NOT text-shadow) because the wordmark uses background-clip:text gradient fill — text-shadow does not render correctly on transparent-fill text; drop-shadow operates on the rendered glyph alpha shape regardless of fill technique. Two stacked drop-shadow layers, matching index.html:534/545-547 exactly:
glow.timing: rest throughout the cycle scene (constant, low-key presence glow even mid-cycle, per the site) -> ramps to peak at t=2.08 (synced with the scale overshoot, same beat) -> eases back to rest by t=2.3 and holds static to the end

exit.choice: clean static hold, no fade-to-black — per dispatch guidance this sting may lead into other clips in the series and should stay loop/cut-friendly
exit.window: 2.3s -> 4.0s (1.7s hold, well past press-release-spring's >=1s climax-dwell constraint)
exit.behavior: wordmark fully settled (scale 1.0, rest glow, STYLE locked pink), zero further motion — deterministic single frame held, no idle loop baked in (kinetic-type-beats' 'Scene N: resolve and HOLD... settle only, no further scale-out' and CTA variant's 'End-card holds dead static' both point the same direction, and it keeps the render trivially seek-safe)

font_embedding.landing_font: "Helvetica Neue" aliases to embedded Inter per typography.md's alias table — pre-bundled, zero network, deterministic, safe for local AND cloud/Lambda renders.
font_embedding.cycle_fonts_status: Of the 9 cycle faces, only Bebas Neue is in HF's pre-bundled/aliased set (Bebas Neue -> League Gothic, pre-bundled, weight 400 — a near-identical visual substitute since League Gothic is metrically close to Bebas Neue, so this alias is effectively lossless). The remaining 8 (Anton, Bungee, Righteous, Permanent Marker, Monoton, Press Start 2P, Alfa Slab One, Pacifico) are NOT in HF's 18-family pre-bundled list — they are kept as-is, unsubstituted, because they are exactly the real fonts the live site already loads via Google Fonts (index.html:9) and the whole concept of this scene IS the visual variety across genuinely different display genres (condensed/grotesque, comic-bold, marker-script, pixel, slab-serif, brush-script); substituting them onto HF's bundled set (which has no comparable variety — only Oswald/League Gothic/Archivo Black as non-banned display options) would gut the shot's entire premise.
font_embedding.caveat_for_builder: Per typography.md, a real Google Font not in the 18-family bundle still renders (HF fetches + embeds it at build time) but (a) trips a font_family_without_font_face lint warning per font — expected here, not a bug — and (b) is fail-closed on distributed/cloud (Lambda) renders if fonts.gstatic.com is unreachable at build time. Recommend a local render for this composition, or confirm network reachability before a cloud render. All 9 names should be written exactly as listed (Google Fonts family names), each with a `,"Anton",sans-serif` fallback chain matching the site's own pattern (index.html:2316) since Anton is already the project's established display fallback.

scenes.motion: single two-line wordmark ('FREESTYLE' / 'LAB') held dead-center; font-family + per-font scale swap every 0.2s via discrete-text-sequence through Anton, Bebas Neue, Bungee, Righteous, Permanent Marker, Monoton, Press Start 2P, Alfa Slab One, Pacifico (in that order, see customize.cycle_sequence) with a hard INSTANT cut on each swap — no crossfade, no tween on the text itself. Color stays neutral paper-gradient throughout (identity of the swap is the shape, not the color). A faint 1.5px shake fires at each swap onset (customize.cycle_sequence.per_swap_jitter) to sell instability. A constant low-key pink glow (customize.glow.rest) sits behind the type the whole scene, per the site reference.

hard cut from Pacifico (last cycle font) into the landing state on the SAME element (no DOM swap) — Helvetica Neue/Arial Bold, uppercase, letter-spacing -0.005em: 'FREE' and 'LAB' in bone white (#F2EEF7), the 'STYLE' substring in stage pink (#FF2E63). Lands with the press-release-spring scale curve (customize.landing_motion: 0.93 dip at cut -> 1.05 overshoot at +0.28s with peak glow -> settle to 1.0 at +0.5s with rest glow), synced 1:1 with the glow ramp (customize.glow). Holds fully static from t=2.3s to the end — clean hold, no fade (customize.exit) — background is #14121A with the 3 very-subtle radial gradients from customize.background (pink top, gold right, green bottom-left), kept low-contrast so the wordmark stays the hero.

shot_brief: A 4-second, 9:16 logo sting for Freestyle Lab. For the first 1.8s, the two-line wordmark 'FREESTYLE / LAB' rapid-cycles through nine distinct display typefaces at 0.2s per font, each swap an instant hard cut with a faint 1-2px jitter — a visual stutter reading as typographic chaos or a battle for identity, held in a single neutral paper-gradient color so the shape-shifting itself is the spectacle, with a constant low-key pink glow underneath. At 1.8s it hard-cuts and locks into the real brand lockup on the same element: 'FREE' and 'LAB' in bone white, 'STYLE' in hot pink, set in uppercase Helvetica Neue/Arial Bold, landing with a press-release-spring scale punch (dip to 0.93, overshoot to 1.05, settle to 1.0 over 0.5s) synced to a glow bloom that peaks at the overshoot and eases to a steady rest glow, then holds clean and fully static through the out — no fade-to-black, since this clip may lead into others in the series. The single dominant motion idea is resolution: visual noise collapsing into a confident, legible brand identity, staged on a near-black background with faint pink/gold/green radial bleed. Tone is freestyle/battle-urban with energy but restraint — punchy, not aggressive.
